questions.scenario: A customer asks the assistant for ITL Pay's fee on a ₦30,000 transfer to another bank. Suppose that, without retrieval, the model answers ₦52.50.
questions.question: Why is this dangerous, and what fixes it?
options: The model knows ITL Pay's fees but rounds them; lower the temperature
The model has never seen ITL Pay's fee table and produces a plausible number; retrieve the fee section and answer only from it
The context window is too small; use a bigger model
The question needs a tool call
questions.explanation: RAG puts your own documents in the prompt so facts come from them, not from training data.

questions.scenario: You switch from nomic-embed-text (768 dimensions) to another embedding model, but keep the existing vector_store rows.
questions.question: What happens?
options: Search keeps working
Only new documents are affected
Old and new vectors can't be compared (and the dimensions may not match): re-embed everything
pgvector converts the vectors automatically
questions.explanation: Vectors are only comparable within one embedding model.

questions.scenario: The help centre is written as pages with '## ' sections, each answering one question.
questions.question: Which chunking strategy suits it best?
options: One chunk per section, prefixed with the page and section titles
Fixed 50-character chunks
One chunk per file
One chunk per sentence
questions.explanation: Structure-aware chunks answer one question each and carry their context.

questions.scenario: ITL Pay's assistant restarts ten times a day. Embedding all documents on each start is slow and, with a hosted model, costs money.
questions.question: What does the starter do?
options: Embeds only on the first day
Embeds documents lazily, at question time
Stores embeddings in Redis
Keeps each file's SHA-256 and re-embeds a file only when its hash changes, deleting its old chunks first
questions.explanation: The help_doc table records the version embedded; unchanged files are skipped.

questions.scenario: The assistant's retriever uses topK(3) and similarityThreshold(0.55).
questions.question: What does the threshold do?
options: Drops chunks less similar to the question than 0.55, so weakly related text isn't sent
Limits the answer to 55% of the context window
Sets the model's temperature
Makes the search exact instead of approximate
questions.explanation: Without a threshold every question gets three chunks, relevant or not.

questions.scenario: allowEmptyContext is true in the starter's ContextualQueryAugmenter.
questions.question: Why?
options: To save tokens
With no matching documents the question may still need a tool, such as a balance lookup, so it goes to the model
Because pgvector can't return empty results
To make answers longer
questions.explanation: The default (false) answers 'I don't know' when nothing is retrieved, which suits a documents-only assistant.

questions.scenario: The assistant gave the ₦25 fee but left out the ₦50 stamp duty that was in the same retrieved chunk.
questions.question: What should you conclude?
options: Retrieval failed
pgvector lost part of the chunk
Answers grounded in the right document can still be incomplete: add the missing fact to the evaluation's expectations
Stamp duty should be removed from the help centre
questions.explanation: Retrieval was right; the generation was incomplete. The evaluation must check the facts that matter.

questions.scenario: The starter's tests use a fake embedding model that hashes words into 768 buckets.
questions.question: What do these tests prove, and what don't they?
options: They prove the real model ranks the right section first
They prove nothing because the embeddings are fake
They prove the chat model's answers are correct
They prove ingestion, re-embedding, retrieval wiring and citations work; ranking quality with the real model is the evaluation's job
questions.explanation: Fakes test your code quickly and repeatably; the evaluation tests quality.
